replies.author: MrNotmark
replies.body:
Three.js is better for quick scenes like this, demos and tech demos work well on three.js
For the AI it is easier to work with three.js because of the insane amount of knowledge that is online about it. But is it better at making games? Are those three.js games good even?
Probably not. Godot or a proper game engine will be miles ahead of theee.js they just need more work.

We used to talk about unreal vs godot/unity a lot back then. The consensus was always that you can build in godot quicker and it is more suitable for solo devs but unreal can create amazing and beautiful open world games, with godot that would be harder.
The same thing is true with three.js but now. Three.js is good if you develop with LLMs but it will hit a limit sooner, you can push godot further and unreal even further but those will require much more work. Unreal I would also not recommend for any solo devs it was made for AAA games honestly

replies.author: Drakim
replies.body:
My own testing has shown that AI agents actually works a lot better with three.js than Godot and Unreal. The existing game engines are somewhat clumsy for the AI agent to work with (although it can use them).

Especially Unreal comes with a lot of bling bling ready out of the box to get a cinematic look that you have to work harder to get with three.js, but it's not impossible.
